{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABdoP9fg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhHI_l8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 250, "title": "Redesign Graph Library with master-detail layout and self-explanatory, low-copy controls", "body": "## Background / UX problem

The current Graph Library UI (introduced in #243 and extended in #247) asks the user to understand implementation terms and read long instructional paragraphs instead of making the intended workflow obvious from **layout, proximity, visual hierarchy and control affordances**.

Observed in `extension/graph-library.html`, `extension/graph-library-page.js`, `extension/graph-library.css`, and shared `extension/app.css`:

- **“Default execution targets”** is jargon. Users simply want to specify *which graph runs in Live* and *which graph drives Web page voice typing*.
- Graph names are rendered as full-width **buttons**, styled globally like input fields. They **look editable**, but clicking them **only selects the graph**. The actual name/description editor lives in **Selected graph**, below the list.
- **Selected graph** and execution target settings are both placed *below* the full list, so the main workflow requires scrolling back and forth. The bottom split uses ~`0.8fr 1.2fr` for configuration/details, not for browsing/selection.
- Dense columns (`Purpose`, `Updated`, `Required models`, `File cache`) and many equally weighted action buttons compete with the essential graph name and Edit action.
- Permanent paragraphs beginning **“OFF by default. Turning ON requests website access to show a mic beside…”** and “File cache status is separate…” are verbose and occupy substantial space even though those details matter only in particular states. Avoid explaining layout with primary/secondary copy; **make the visual grouping convey the meaning**.

## Desired design: graph list left; selected graph details right

**Implement this proposed layout**, not another long block of instructions:

```text
Graph Library                        [+ New graph]
[ Search graphs… ]     [sort/filter as lightweight controls]

┌──────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┐
│ Graphs                   │ Voice Input                    │
│                          │ [Graph preview]                │
│ ▸ Voice Input            │ [Edit graph]  [Duplicate] [⋯]  │
│   · Web voice typing     │                                │
│   Meeting Notes          │ Name: [Voice Input          ]  │
│   · Live                 │ Description: […]               │
│   Translation            │ [Save details]                 │
│                          │                                │
│                          │ Use this graph for             │
│                          │ Live   [Set as Live graph]     │
│                          │ Web voice [Assigned ✓]         │
└──────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┘

Web page voice typing    [ON/OFF]     Using: Voice Input
```

The wireframe is conceptual; refine spacing and visual polish, but retain the structure and interaction hierarchy.

### A. Left: graph selection, NOT a misleading form

- Make the list rows read as **selectable items** (plain name/row, clear selected highlight, hover/focus/keyboard state), not text input fields and not bordered full-width form-like buttons. Keep accessible button/listbox semantics as appropriate.
- Show compact **Live** and **Web voice typing** assignment indicators on corresponding graph rows. No raw graph IDs, verbose per-row help text or gratuitous status badges.
- Preserve search/sort/filter, empty state, and distinct invalid/recovery state, but prioritize the **name**; move less-frequently used model/cache metadata to the right-hand details or on-demand details. Avoid a 5-column pseudo-form.
- Selection immediately updates the right panel. Clearly separate **select**, **rename**, **open Graph Editor**, and **use this graph**.

### B. Right: one coherent selected-graph detail panel

- Show selected graph name as the heading plus a readable preview.
- Primary action: **Edit graph** (opens Graph Editor for that graph); adjacent **Duplicate**. Group low-frequency **Export JSON / Delete / Check model files** under a discoverable **⋯ (More)** menu, with proper disabled reasons/confirmations.
- Expose name and description as **actual editable fields** *in the detail panel*, with a clearly labeled Save action and unsaved-change handling; do not confuse these with editing the graph's nodes. Support existing Load saved details/recovery paths, perhaps as a secondary action rather than equal prominence.
- Visually group graph-specific target assignment under **“Use this graph for”**:
  - **Live**: indicate whether this graph is currently the Live default; if not, offer **Use for Live / Set as Live graph**. Live must always have exactly one valid assigned graph.
  - **Web voice typing**: show whether this graph is currently assigned; if eligible and not assigned, offer **Use for Web voice typing**. Provide a way to unassign. A graph that is incompatible (see `webVoiceError`) must not be assignable; show a short actionable reason **on attempted action / hover / expandable details**, not an essay in every list option.
- Selection is **not** automatic target assignment. Changing assignments affects only subsequent sessions; retain running session snapshots.

### C. Global Web voice ON/OFF: obvious and separate from assignment

- Put one compact, clearly labeled **Web voice typing** ON/OFF control (e.g. under the main two-pane area) with the **currently assigned graph's name** beside it, so it is obvious this is a **global feature switch**, not a per-graph switch on the selected item.
- Keep assignment and consent **independent**: choosing a graph does **not** enable website injection, and turning OFF does **not** lose the graph assignment.
- Remove the currently **permanently displayed explanatory paragraphs** from the normal Library view. Default OFF can be communicated by the switch's actual OFF state. If no eligible graph is assigned, show a compact required action instead of a paragraph.
- **Progressive disclosure for real decisions:** display **concise permission rationale and scope when clicking ON**, immediately before invoking Chrome's native permission flow; if the user needs more detail, provide a discreet Help/info disclosure. Show targeted error/recovery messages only when relevant (host denial, missing permission, incompatible graph, model failure).
- The important security facts must remain discoverable and accessible, not silently omitted: which website permission is requested, why, mic capture only on click, and how to disable/revoke. Do not assume visual layout alone substitutes for screen-reader semantics, explicit permission consent or actionable errors.

## Design principles

**Show the workflow through spatial arrangement, not a wall of labels.**

- Strong information hierarchy: find/select graph → inspect/edit → assign use → optionally enable Web voice.
- Group related controls by proximity and alignment; clear selection/assignment/enablement differences.
- Prefer concise labels, recognizable affordances and contextual feedback to repetitive explanatory/secondary text.
- Primary action visually dominant; secondary actions quiet; destructive/rare actions placed intentionally, not crowded beside the main action.
- No removal of legally/security-relevant disclosures, critical error messages or accessibility names simply to reduce copy. Put them at the point of need (progressive disclosure).

## Compatibility / constraints

- Preserve existing `GraphLibrary` persistence, stable graph IDs, revisions/locking/conflict and legacy recovery, import/export, validation, graph preview, search/filter/sort, model file cache inspection, and multi-tab updates. **This is a UI/UX redesign, not a data/schema migration**.
- Preserve existing Live and Web voice assignment semantics, `webVoiceError` eligibility and permission-gated `chrome.storage.local` opt-in; no changes to live capture or ASR/model inference.
- Make selection and detail editing safe: no loss of dirty name/description on switching rows, filtering, async updates or browser refresh; same conflict/recovery guarantees as current code.
- Responsive behavior: true side-by-side master/detail on wide windows; on narrow widths use a legible stacked or selection→detail layout with an obvious Back to graphs action, not squeezed mini-columns or giant paragraphs. Keyboard/focus/ARIA labeling and mobile/small-screen zoom should remain usable.
- Match existing app's visual language, spacing, borders and typography; reduce decorative boxes and redundant words, not useful discoverability.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Wide screen: **list left / selected graph detail right**; selecting another graph immediately updates the right panel without a long vertical trip.
- [ ] Graph names in the list **look like selectable rows, not text inputs**; actual rename fields live only within the detail editor, with clear save and unsaved changes.
- [ ] “Default execution targets” wording and its standalone old settings block are **removed**. The UI naturally conveys setting a selected graph for **Live** or **Web voice typing**.
- [ ] Compact Live/Web assignment markers appear in the list and selected graph details; selections remain distinct from assignments and active running sessions.
- [ ] Web voice ON/OFF is clearly **global** and its assigned graph is visible; initially OFF when not opted in; permissions requested only on explicit enable, with concise **just-in-time** explanation rather than permanent copy.
- [ ] Long permanent copy (“OFF by default. Turning ON requests website access…” etc. and cache/preparation explanations) is removed from default view and moved to appropriate conditional help/permission/error states without loss of accessibility, consent or safety.
- [ ] Main action is **Edit graph**; Duplicate easy to find; Export/Delete/Check model files discoverable under ⋯ or appropriate contextual menu, with existing safety guards.
- [ ] Existing target assignment, compatibility validation, data conflict protection, deleted-graph guards, graph operations, imports/exports and model cache status still work.
- [ ] Good responsive + keyboard + screen-reader affordances; no critical information conveyed by color alone. No regressions to Live/Graph Editor/Web voice runtime.
- [ ] Update browser UI interaction and responsive screenshot/visual tests (where practical), docs/screenshots, and report tests run.

## Scope

Only **Graph Library UI/UX** (HTML/JS/CSS and relevant tests/docs), not the in-page mic icon styling (separate #249), not graph execution, and not new site-specific permissions or feature behavior.
